content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: a no-cost rebalance that lifts the 12:45-15:15 service level to 84.7%, above the 80% target.","why":"A sickness wave, mostly dengue logged between 06:31 and 09:44, has left payments at 33 agents against 39 planned and general at 27 against 33. Call volume and handle times are close to forecast, so this is a capacity gap, not a demand spike. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just clear target at 82.8%, which leaves little margin. P1 costs nothing and gives more headroom. It delays the 12:45-13:15 breaks in both queues by 30 minutes, moves cross-skilled agents between queues as each one peaks, and switches on IVR callback on payments from 13:00 to 15:00. That raises payments to 85.2% and general to 84.0%, cuts predicted abandons from 3.4% to 2.9%, and brings rest-of-day service to 92.9%. No policy is breached.","trade_offs":["P3 (overtime plus free levers) reaches 86.9% with 2.4% abandons but costs INR 2,160. That is about 2 points more for spend the target does not need.","P4 (overtime only) reaches 86.0% for INR 5,040. It is the most expensive option, and general only gets to 84.7%.","P2 costs INR 942 yet scores lower than P1 overall at 83.9%. It also leaves general close to target at 80.9%, so it shifts risk onto the general queue.","P1 depends on agents accepting delayed breaks and on callback take-up, rather than on paid extra staff."],"watch":"Watch both queues as the 2 agents leave payments for general (13:00-14:00) and the 3 return from general to payments (14:00-15:00), making sure neither queue drops toward 80%. If more sick calls come in, be ready to offer overtime as in P3."}
